title: How many training credits do certified accountants need each year in Portugal?
description: Portugal's Ordem dos Contabilistas Certificados requires 30 training credits a year under Regulamento 352/2024: how credits are earned and enforced.
shortAnswer: Certified accountants (contabilistas certificados) with active registration in Portugal must complete and justify at least 30 continuing professional training credits per year, or a proportional amount for part of a year, under Regulamento n.º 352/2024 of the Ordem dos Contabilistas Certificados (OCC). One credit is awarded per hour of training. Failing to meet the training obligation, as provided in article 70(5) of the OCC Statute, prevents the accountant from practicing until it is met.
keyTakeaways: Article 5(2) of Regulamento n.º 352/2024 requires at least 30 continuing training credits each year, pro rated for the period of practice in that year.
Training should cover accounting, taxation, ethics and deontology, and law in the accountant's areas of activity (article 4(1)).
The OCC Board (Conselho Diretivo) can now make a specific course or subject mandatory for all certified accountants (articles 4(2) and 5(3)).

Credits: 1 per training hour; 30 for passing at least 25% of curricular units in a degree or postgraduate program in a year; 6 per technical article; 16 per scientific journal article; 30 per scientific book; 6 per exam jury.
Non-compliance prevents practice automatically once the deadline for credit attribution passes (article 10), and breach of the regulation is a disciplinary offense (article 12).
regulator: Ordem dos Contabilistas Certificados (OCC), the public professional association for certified accountants
appliesTo: Certified accountants (contabilistas certificados) with active OCC registration who practice under article 10 of the OCC Statute
Accounting firms and professional companies that employ certified accountants
Training providers, universities and professional bodies delivering training for OCC credit
Certified accountants who teach, publish or sit on OCC exam juries

sections.heading: What continuing training does the OCC require?

blocks.text: The OCC requires each practicing certified accountant to complete and justify at least 30 continuing training credits per year. Article 5(2) of the [Regulamento de Formação Profissional Contínua](https://www.occ.pt/pt-pt/ordem/regulamentos/regulamento-de-formacao-profissional-continua) states that certified accountants "são obrigados a realizar e a justificar, no mínimo, um total de 30 créditos de formação profissional contínua por ano ou um proporcional em relação ao período em que exerceram a atividade nesse ano" (are required to complete and justify a minimum of 30 continuing training credits per year, or a proportional amount for the period in which they practiced that year).

The regulation applies to certified accountants with active registration who practice the profession under article 10 of the Estatuto da Ordem dos Contabilistas Certificados (EOCC). It was approved as Regulamento n.º 352/2024, signed on March 15, 2024, following amendments to the OCC Statute by Lei n.º 68/2023 of December 7, which aligned it with Lei n.º 12/2023 on public professional associations. It enters into force on the day after publication in the Diário da República.

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects Regulamento n.º 352/2024 as published on the OCC website as at November 2026. Translations from Portuguese are unofficial.

sections.heading: Which subjects must OCC training cover?

blocks.text: Training should cover, among other subjects, accounting, taxation, ethics and deontology, and law in the areas where certified accountants work, plus related professional matters (article 4(1)). The stated objectives in article 3 include maintaining public confidence in the profession, ensuring respect for ethical and deontological rules, and keeping accountants current with the regulatory framework for their work.

The main change in the 2024 regulation is that the OCC Board can make a specific training course or subject compulsory for every certified accountant where it considers this fundamental to practice (article 4(2)). Article 5(3) then obliges accountants to attend and pass that training. In exceptional, justified circumstances, or on a justified request from the accountant, the Board may waive the annual credit obligation in a specific case (article 5(4)).

The OCC must publish an annual continuing training plan by the end of November of the preceding year, listing topics, type of training, syllabus content and short profiles of trainers and authors of materials (article 11). Firms can use that plan as an input to their own [training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix).

sections.heading: How are OCC training credits earned?

blocks.text: Credits come from attending or delivering training, academic study, publishing and exam jury service. Article 6 lists the routes and article 7 sets the credit values.

blocks.text: Training delivered under the Labor Code route links OCC credits to employers' statutory training duty, covered on the page about [Portugal Labor Code continuous training](/regulations/portugal-labour-code-continuous-training). A firm that runs certified in-house sessions can therefore count the same hours toward both obligations where the content qualifies.

sections.heading: How are credits claimed and how is non-OCC training certified?

blocks.text: For routes other than OCC's own training, the accountant (or the training provider, if agreed) must send proof of completion and, where relevant, of passing to the OCC by the end of the first quarter of the following year (article 8(1)). Requests are made through the means provided on the OCC website (article 8(2)).

Providers that are not certified must ask the OCC to certify a course at least 30 days before it runs (article 9(1)). The request must include the title, dates, duration, topic, detailed program, trainers and their credentials, location, capacity and equipment, materials and any assessment method. The OCC weighs the topic's usefulness for the profession, the program's fit with the topic, trainers' scientific, technical and teaching qualifications, and delivery conditions. It responds within 15 days, and if it does not decide in that time the course is treated as authorized (articles 9(4) and 9(5)). Certification requests are subject to the fee in the OCC fee regulation.

sections.heading: What happens if a certified accountant does not meet the OCC training requirement?

blocks.text: The accountant is prevented from practicing. Article 10(2) states that failing the training obligations, as provided in article 70(5) of the OCC Statute, "impede o contabilista certificado de exercer a atividade" (prevents the certified accountant from practicing), and article 10(3) makes the impediment start automatically once the article 8 deadline for claiming credits has passed.

Article 10(1) makes each accountant responsible for their own training. Under article 12, any certified accountant who intentionally or negligently breaches the regulation's obligations commits a disciplinary offense. For firms, this means CPD gaps are a business continuity risk: an accountant who signs returns or accounts for clients cannot do so while the impediment applies. The guide on [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) sets out a general evidence approach.

sections.heading: How does the OCC requirement compare with other accounting bodies?

blocks.text: The OCC uses an annual credit target rather than a triennium. Thirty credits a year is comparable in annual terms to the 120 hours per three years required by [CPA Australia](/regulations/cpa-australia-cpd-requirements) and CA ANZ, but there is no multi-year averaging, so a shortfall in one year triggers the practice impediment. The preamble to the regulation says it was drafted with regard to standards defined internationally by the International Federation of Accountants (IFAC).

Portuguese accounting firms also have AML duties that require staff training; see [Portugal AML law training requirements](/regulations/portugal-aml-law-training-requirements). Groups with accountants in several countries can compare the [US CPA CPE requirements](/regulations/us-cpa-cpe-requirements), and the [professional services industry page](/industries/professional-services) explains how Knowledge Foundry supports firms across these markets.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records the article 6 route, credit value and evidence for each activity, and flags external training that still needs to be submitted before the first quarter deadline. For in-house programs it holds the program, trainer profiles and assessment method that an article 9 certification request requires.

faqs.q: Do part-year certified accountants need the full 30 credits?
faqs.a: No. Article 5(2) of Regulamento n.º 352/2024 allows a proportional amount relative to the period in which the accountant practiced during the year, so someone who registers or resumes practice mid-year needs fewer credits.

faqs.q: Can a postgraduate course satisfy the OCC requirement?
faqs.a: Yes. Passing, or teaching, at least 25% of the curricular units in a year of a degree, postgraduate, master's or doctoral program in areas listed in article 17 of the OCC Statute earns 30 credits, which meets the annual minimum on its own.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to submit external training to the OCC?
faqs.a: Proof of external training, publications or jury service must reach the OCC by the end of the first quarter of the year following the activity. After that deadline, an accountant without enough credits is automatically prevented from practicing.

faqs.q: Can the OCC require a specific course for everyone?
faqs.a: Yes. Since Regulamento n.º 352/2024, the OCC Board can decide that a particular training course or subject is mandatory for all certified accountants where it is considered fundamental to practice, and accountants must attend and pass it.

factCheck.claim: Article 5(2): minimum 30 continuing training credits per year or proportional to period of practice
Article 4(1) subjects include accounting, taxation, ethics and deontology and law; article 4(2) and 5(3) allow the Conselho Diretivo to make specific training mandatory
Article 7 credits: 1 per hour; 30 for at least 25% of curricular units; 6 per technical article; 16 per scientific journal article; 30 per scientific book; 6 per exam jury participation
Article 8: proof of external credits sent by end of first quarter of following year
Article 9: non-certified providers request certification at least 30 days before; OCC responds within 15 days; silence counts as authorization
Article 10(2)-(3): non-compliance under EOCC article 70(5) prevents practice, starting automatically after the article 8 deadline; article 12 disciplinary offense
Article 11: OCC publishes annual training plan by end of November of the preceding year
Regulation approved following Lei n.º 68/2023 of 7 December amending the EOCC; signed 15 March 2024 by the Bastonária
